data_evidence.role: exact one-shot and binary-consumer identification cases

exact_consequences: The complete one-shot lexical law is exactly independent of the MPARSE parameter p.
The binary structural-versus-null response has a second-difference sign boundary at p=m(n+1).
The same one-shot lexical law is therefore compatible with positive, zero, and negative binary-response curvature.
One independently warranted binary response at known n recovers p through p=mn+logit(r_n).
no_conclusion_if: the binary response task or its grammar-to-response bridge is absent
the one-shot consumer is redefined to include an observed null candidate
separate binary responses are treated as one normalized lexical distribution
nonclaims: Lexical absence is not treated as an observed null-candidate response.
The formal recovery equation does not warrant any particular experimental response bridge.
No universal phonotactic architecture is selected.
registered_query: consumer-relative identification of MPARSE and curvature of the binary response
scope: The source's printed one-shot lexical normalizer and separate structural-versus-null binary competitions.
title_pt_BR: Não identificação e recuperação de MPARSE relativas ao consumidor
withdrawal_condition: Withdraw or narrow the application if MPARSE enters the authoritative one-shot normalizer or if the claimed observations already include an independently calibrated binary channel.
